scope: Same first four BY2 raw blocks, causal100.0 s navigation prefix only. Broadcast-state/measurement algebra calculations; no navigation estimation, new integer enumeration, reference, Q changes or threshold changes.

derivation.receiver_clock_cancellation: With T_r=t_r+dt_r and P_r=rho_r+c(dt_r-dt_sat)+propagation/code terms, T_r-P_r/c cancels receiver clock. RTKLIB satposs then subtracts broadcast satellite clock once. Subtracting receiver clock again would double-correct.
derivation.implemented_known_sd: range(sat2_at_own_transmit,anchor)-range(sat1_at_own_transmit,anchor)-c*(satclock2-satclock1), using geometric Earth-rotation flight delay once.
derivation.corrected_phase_model: After removing DD(known_sd), first-order raw DD phase is B*[p_ant2(t2)-p_ant1(t1)]+lambda*N.
derivation.same_time_approximation_remainder: For desired instantaneous baseline b(t1), p_ant2(t2)-p_ant1(t1)=b(t1)+v_ant2(t1)*(t2-t1)+O(dt^2). The first-order remainder is B*v_ant2*dt.
derivation.free_baseline_invariance: For each N and any displacement d, min_b ||y-B*d-A*N-B*b||_Q^2 = min_b ||y-A*N-B*b||_Q^2. The Gaussian relaxed domain allows an independent3D baseline per epoch, so this first-order displacement cannot change its emptiness.
derivation.doppler_comparison: The raw DD Doppler times common clock-skew proxy contains satellite motion as well as receiver motion. Subtract the already-implemented known DD before judging an omitted term. Applying the full Doppler alignment on top of existing known_sd would double-count satellite motion.
derivation.timing_proxy_boundary: Minus median((P2-P1-known_sd)/c) diagnoses relative receive time under the short-baseline RAWX clock convention. It retains baseline/code/atmosphere/hardware uncertainty and is not an independent receiver synchronization calibration.

conclusion.source_cache_geometry_reproduction: All admitted SD known_sd values exactly reproduced using the same causal prefix and broadcast provider.
conclusion.relaxed_empty_explanation: No omitted identified common time/clock term explains EMPTY_RELAXED_SUPPORT. The major satellite term is already removed; first-order receiver displacement is inside the existing free-baseline nuisance subspace.
conclusion.shared_graph_approximation: Instantaneous rigid baseline remains an approximation for asynchronous physical antenna samples. A future source-calibrated model could use p(t2)+R(t2)*l2-p(t1)-R(t1)*l1, or its IMU-derived first-order equivalent, rather than adding a full raw Doppler time shift. This is not demonstrated as the cause or remedy of the current empty relaxed domain.
conclusion.small_residual_boundary: The remaining Doppler-minus-known template includes Doppler noise, code-derived timing uncertainty and linearization error; it is not a calibrated correction. Its nonzero projected component is quantified only. No outside-domain global integer minimum was computed, so no numerical claim is made that an arbitrarily small non-B perturbation could never change a boundary case.
